Real twilight, not a virtual sky

Virtual twilight has gotten good enough to fool a quick scroll. An editor takes a two o'clock exterior, swaps in a purple sky, and turns the windows on digitally. It costs almost nothing and it looks almost right, which is exactly the problem: the light on the house still comes from overhead at midday, the windows glow without anything lighting the room behind them, and the shadows point the wrong way.

Real twilight is a second visit at blue hour with the house lit. The light is genuinely coming from where it appears to come from, so the frame holds up at full screen on a tablet at nine at night — which is exactly when and how buyers are looking. For the side-by-side, see the real twilight page.

Scheduling the blue-hour window in West Michigan

Blue hour is short and it moves all year. In West Michigan the usable window runs roughly twenty to forty minutes after sunset, which in late June means shooting close to ten at night and in December means being set up before five in the afternoon. That is the practical scheduling note for a Comstock Park listing: in summer the twilight visit is late, in winter it is early, and in both cases it is a narrow window that has to be booked rather than squeezed in.

Because the window is short, the house needs to be ready before it opens: interior lights on throughout, landscape and porch lighting on, garage lit, blinds set, and cars moved. A twilight frame is largely made in the fifteen minutes of preparation before the light arrives.

Comstock Park twilight photography FAQ

How much does real twilight cost in Comstock Park?
$150 as an add-on to the Essential tier ($245), and included free in Showcase ($375) and Signature ($525).

Is this a real shoot or an edited sky?
A real shoot. It is a separate visit at blue hour with the house lit, not a daytime exterior with a sky replaced in post.

When would you shoot a Comstock Park listing at twilight?
Roughly twenty to forty minutes after sunset, which shifts across the year — close to ten at night in late June, before five in the afternoon in December.

What does the seller need to do?
